name: Electric-Assist Bicycle
description: A single category, not the three-class system: a low-speed electrically assisted bicycle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts that assists only while the rider pedals, to a top motor-powered speed under 20 mph. It's regulated as a bicycle.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts (one horsepower) (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
Top motor-powered speed under 20 mph, measured with a 170-pound rider on a paved level surface (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
No throttle: the motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
No class system: South Carolina has not adopted the three-class model law
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently label it with its wattage and top assisted speed; owners may not remove or tamper with the label (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
Anyone who modifies it to change its speed must replace the label to match (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
Carries only as many riders as it's designed and equipped for
Treated as a bicycle, not a moped: no driver's license, registration or insurance (South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29))
Rides by the same rules as a bicycle, including using an adjacent bicycle lane where one is provided (South Carolina Code §56-5-3520)
One whose motor exceeds 750 W, up to 1,500 W, is a moped, which needs a driver's or moped license and registration
